prompt:
A densely annotated editorial infographic plate, drawn by hand in confident ink
line with light watercolour and gouache wash on bright warm-white paper.
Contour line varies in weight and is charcoal near-black. Dimensional but not
photographic: restrained hatching, subtle texture, believable volume, selective
shadow, clean uncluttered background. Every material reads as itself — dull grey
lead, unglazed earthenware, weathered timber, damp fibrous bark — and materials
that differ in the explanation look visibly different. Quiet palette of stone,
clay, wood, and metal tones over the warm-white ground, with one or two
desaturated accents that each keep a single meaning throughout the plate.
Contemporary editorial typography: one calm display face for the title, one
highly legible face for the many small labels, sentence case, crisply printed
and correctly spelled. Annotation is dense and disciplined — leader lines,
brackets, dimension marks, magnified inset circles, small side studies — laid
out so no two leaders cross. Asymmetric composition with about a quarter of the
page left quiet. Modern printing on clean stock: fresh, crisp, and unaged. The
only lettering anywhere on the plate is the title, the deck, the labels, and the
short notes. The words hero, drawing, figure, plate, inset, zone, band, strip,
trio, column, and cutaway describe the construction of the page and are never
lettered onto it, alone or in a phrase: no headings that name parts of the
layout, no percentages or
proportions of the page, no tags in brackets after a label or note, no sentence
describing the drawing or explaining what the reader is meant to see, no
signature, monogram, date, watermark, or credit line.

The plate is headed "pipeline", with the standing line "An essay mill that moves every idea stub through research, outline, draft and factcheck, one stage per cycle, under a live dashboard." beneath it.

The dominant picture, filling roughly half the page, shows A long mill track of six stations running left to right: pending, research, outline, draft, factcheck, done. At far left, project folders from projects feed thin essay stubs onto the track. Each essay is a folder that thickens station by station as stage files accumulate inside it. A clock escapement above the track advances essays one notch per tick. Every station is fed by the same single writing model, a pen on a gantry above the track. All motion runs rightward.

Magnified circles set beside it show circle one, an essay folder's .meta.yaml tag recording status and accumulated cost, which is why the mill can stop and resume. circle two, the escapement tooth, one notch every 15 seconds. circle three, a broken cable with a retry notice, showing how the dashboard reports API retries. studies are a dashboard page with Resume and Step buttons and an interval dial, a scrolling running log, and a hand pressing Ctrl-C three times.

Colour is used so that Warm red marks forward advancement, meaning the notch each essay moves this cycle. Green marks money, meaning accumulated and total cost. Blue marks human control, meaning pause, resume, step and interrupt.

Draw these quantities as dimension marks or counts: Six stations from pending to done. One stage per cycle. 15-second default cycle interval. Two spend tiers, cheap and pro. Third Ctrl-C press force-quits.

These trade words appear on the plate, each set against the thing it names: pending, research, outline, draft and factcheck sit on their five stations, and done sits on the final stack. projects sits on the feeding folders, and .meta.yaml on each essay's tag. compose model sits on the pen gantry, and dashboard on the control page. Resume and Step sit on its buttons, cycle interval on the dial, and running log on the scroll. Ctrl-C sits on the pressed key and API retry on the broken cable. config.yaml sits on the settings sheet in the foot. --dry-run, --once and --spend sit on their switches, with cheap and pro on the two spend positions. model registry sits on the price ledger. total cost sits on the final summary.

Letter these words onto the drawings, spelled exactly as given: pending, research, outline, draft, factcheck, done, projects, essay stub, compose model. .meta.yaml, accumulated cost, every 15 seconds, API retry. dashboard, Resume, Step, cycle interval, running log, Ctrl-C. factchecked essays, per-project summary, total cost. config.yaml, --dry-run, --once, --spend, cheap, pro, model registry.

Set these short notes beside what they explain: Each cycle moves essays one stage forward; Stubs from scaffold start at pending. State lives in each project folder; Stop anytime, resume where it left. The mill starts paused until Resume; Third Ctrl-C force-quits. Shutdown prints each project's final tally. Dry run: full machinery, no API calls; Prices come from the model registry.
